metadata.title: Is AI's 'capex tsunami' the catalyst for the next big credit boom?

content.text:
00:00 Speaker A
Most credit booms are caused by a huge wave of capital expenditures, a capex wave, a tsunami. That's what you had in 99. That's what you had in 2005 to 2007, and that's what you have right now. But it's a cycle. And there will be pockets of the market where the unprofitable projects will eventually, the let the debt holders will have to pay the price.
00:33 Speaker B
Yeah, right.
00:34 Speaker A
Now the question is, will will those debt holders actually be hedged against that?
00:40 Speaker B
Right.
00:40 Speaker A
And that's the big question.
00:41 Speaker B
Right.
00:42 Speaker A
What I'm suggesting is that the corporate balance sheets, you're right, are pretty clean. A lot of it's being pushed out into the investor class buyer beware if you're an insurance company or whatnot, okay, from that perspective, but it's more the speculative holders that may take the hit on that.
01:07 Speaker B
Right.
01:08 Speaker A
So that is a leverage issue. And then you have the question of the cash market, that's the long only stock investors, and the non-cash market, which is the futures markets with perpetuals and all the other stuff that we're that have become quite popular today. And I'm just suggesting that that right tail risk we're really out there on that side, which you have to just be somewhat mindful. Again, we're bullish long run. We think high quality stocks are the place to be, stay away from the high momentum stocks.
01:46 Speaker B
Well, Sammy, let me ask you this. You see Alphabet reporting its first quarter of negative free cash flow since going public. Does that worry you?
01:58 Speaker A
It doesn't really worry me because again, you have such strong balance sheets there in a pretty good spot. I I go back to first principles. I mean, you're supposed to get to an optimal capital structure.
02:12 Speaker B
Right.
02:12 Speaker A
So, zero debt is generally not an optimal capital structure. We still have, there's little constraints around tax deductibility, but it's still, that you still can deduct a lot of the interest expense. So companies should have debt. So to some extent, it's it's a maturation of the tech sector and the semiconductor space to have some reasonable amount of debt, because that's the right answer for ultimately the equity shareholders at the bottom of the at the bottom of the of the stack.
